title: Tune claude.md files and prompts
task_breakdown_summary: Three phases with 12 tasks total. Phase 1 (content audit) addresses quality/correctness with 5 tasks across 2 PRs. Phase 2 (role-based filtering) addresses token efficiency with 3 tasks in 1 PR. Phase 3 (prompt unification) moves GHA prompt generation into Python with 4 tasks across 2 PRs. Each phase is independently valuable and results in a working, tested system.

phases.name: Content Audit & Quality
phases.goal: Ensure all prompt content is correct, concise, and appropriate for its audience. No structural changes—content only.
phases.priority: P0 — addresses the issue's primary concern (quality and correctness)
phases.pr_strategy: 2 PRs: one for CLAUDE.md rule file content (T1-T2), one for prompt builder quality (T3-T5)

tasks.title: Audit and tighten mission.md content
tasks.description: Review sandbox/.claude/rules/mission.md for redundancy and conciseness. Remove content that duplicates orchestrator phase prompts (e.g., workflow overview that's already in _build_phase_prompt). Tighten wording throughout. Ensure the non-interactive mode section accurately reflects current GHA execution. Do NOT split the file yet (that's Phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: mission.md reduced by at least 15 lines without losing essential guidance
No content duplicates what _build_phase_prompt() or _build_agent_prompt() already provides
All remaining instructions are accurate for the current codebase
No behavioral regression: agents still receive all necessary operational instructions

tasks.title: Audit and trim orchestrator.md
tasks.description: Review sandbox/.claude/rules/orchestrator.md. Most egg-orch CLI commands are used by the orchestrator service itself, not by agents. Trim to only the commands agents actually use: primarily `egg-orch signal` (progress, complete, error, heartbeat) and references to `egg-contract`. Remove the full CLI reference table—it belongs in developer docs, not agent context. Keep the environment variables section but trim to what's relevant.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator.md reduced by at least 40 lines
Only agent-relevant commands remain (signal, contract references, health check)
Full CLI reference removed or replaced with a 1-line pointer to docs
Environment variables section trimmed to runtime-relevant vars only
No behavioral regression for agents that do use egg-orch commands

tasks.title: Enrich orchestrator role prompts with command-file guidance
tasks.description: Compare _build_agent_prompt() role-specific sections in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py against the richer slash command definitions in sandbox/.claude/commands/ (coder-mode.md, tester-mode.md, documenter-mode.md, integrator-mode.md). The orchestrator role prompts are very brief (10-15 lines each) while command files have significantly more behavioral guidance. Identify key guidance missing from orchestrator prompts and incorporate it. Do NOT simply copy command files—extract the essential behavioral instructions that improve agent output quality.
acceptance_criteria: Each role prompt in _build_agent_prompt() includes key behavioral guidance from corresponding command file
Orchestrator role prompts remain concise (no more than 2x current length per role)
No contradictions between orchestrator prompts and command file definitions
Existing orchestrator prompt tests updated to reflect new content
All existing tests pass
tasks.estimated_scope: medium — one file modified, multiple sections, test updates

tasks.title: Incorporate conventions into orchestrator prompt builders
tasks.description: The GHA prompt scripts load conventions files (review-conventions.md, autofixer-conventions.md, conflict-conventions.md) that provide detailed behavioral guidance, but the orchestrator prompt builders don't use them. Ensure the orchestrator's _build_review_prompt() and _build_autofix_prompt() load and include the same conventions. Use the existing _read_shared_criteria() pattern to load conventions from action/ directory or embed the key guidance directly.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator review prompt includes conventions equivalent to review-conventions.md content
Orchestrator autofix prompt includes conventions equivalent to autofixer-conventions.md content
Conventions loading follows the existing _read_shared_criteria() pattern (file-based, overridable)
Existing orchestrator prompt tests updated
All tests pass
tasks.estimated_scope: medium — one file modified, conventions loading added, test updates

tasks.title: Verify GHA prompt quality and align with orchestrator
tasks.description: Review each GHA bash script (build-review-prompt.sh, build-autofixer-prompt.sh, build-agent-mode-design-review-prompt.sh, build-contract-verification-prompt.sh) for quality. Ensure inline fallback criteria still match the shared/prompts/ files. Verify the prompt structure produces appropriate output. Fix any quality issues found. Also ensure the command files (sandbox/.claude/commands/*.md) don't contradict the orchestrator prompt instructions from T3.
acceptance_criteria: All inline fallback criteria in GHA scripts match their shared/prompts/ counterparts
Command file definitions don't contradict orchestrator prompt instructions
Any discrepancies between command files and orchestrator prompts are resolved (one source of truth)
GHA script prompt output is clean and well-structured
All existing action tests pass
tasks.estimated_scope: medium — multiple files reviewed and potentially edited

phases.name: Role-Based CLAUDE.md Filtering
phases.goal: Reduce irrelevant context per agent by assembling CLAUDE.md based on agent role. Only pipeline agents are affected; interactive (no-role) sessions get the full CLAUDE.md.
phases.priority: P1 — addresses token efficiency (issue's secondary concern)
phases.pr_strategy: 1 PR for the complete filtering implementation (T6-T8)

tasks.title: Split mission.md into composable rule files
tasks.description: Split sandbox/.claude/rules/mission.md into 3 files: (1) mission-core.md (~50 lines): role definition, decision framework, git safety, quality—universal to all agents. (2) mission-workflow.md (~60 lines): PR lifecycle, commit workflow, cross-contamination prevention, review responses—coder/refiner only. (3) mission-ci.md (~25 lines): non-interactive mode, notifications—GHA execution only. Delete the original mission.md after splitting. Ensure concatenation of all 3 files produces equivalent content to the original.
acceptance_criteria: Original mission.md deleted
Three new files created with clear, non-overlapping content boundaries
Concatenation of all 3 files (in order: core, workflow, ci) covers all content from original
Each file has a clear audience comment at the top (e.g., '# Universal' / '# Coder/Refiner only')
No content lost in the split
tasks.estimated_scope: small — file split, no logic changes

tasks.title: Implement role-based rules_order in setup_agent_rules()
tasks.description: Modify setup_agent_rules() in sandbox/entrypoint.py to read EGG_AGENT_ROLE and select appropriate rule files per role. Define a ROLE_RULES mapping dict. When no role is set (interactive use), use the full file set for backward compatibility. The mapping should be: coder gets all files; tester gets core+environment+code-standards+test-workflow; reviewer/architect/task_planner/risk_analyst/documenter get core+environment; integrator gets core+environment+code-standards+test-workflow; checker gets core+environment+code-standards+test-workflow. Pipeline-conditional rules (contract.md, orchestrator.md) remain gated on EGG_PIPELINE_ID but are also role-filtered (only coder/tester/integrator/refiner get contract.md).
acceptance_criteria: setup_agent_rules() reads EGG_AGENT_ROLE environment variable
ROLE_RULES mapping covers all AgentRole enum values
Default (no role) produces the same CLAUDE.md as before the change
Each role gets only the rule files relevant to its responsibilities
Pipeline-conditional rules (contract.md, orchestrator.md) respect both EGG_PIPELINE_ID and role
Function is well-documented with rationale for the mapping
tasks.estimated_scope: medium — one function modified with new branching logic

tasks.title: Add tests for role-based CLAUDE.md assembly
tasks.description: Create comprehensive test coverage for the new role-based filtering in setup_agent_rules(). Test each role gets the correct file set. Test the default (no role) case produces the full set. Test pipeline vs non-pipeline conditional inclusion. Test unknown role values fall back to the default set.
files_to_create_or_modify: tests for sandbox/entrypoint.py — check existing test structure to determine location
acceptance_criteria: Test coverage for every role in the AgentRole enum
Test for default/no-role case (backward compatibility)
Test for unknown role fallback
Test for pipeline-conditional rules (contract.md, orchestrator.md) inclusion/exclusion
Tests verify actual file content assembly, not just file list selection
All tests pass

phases.name: Prompt Generation Unification
phases.goal: Move GHA prompt generation into a shared Python module so both execution paths (GHA and orchestrator) use the same prompt generators. Bash scripts become thin wrappers.
phases.priority: P2 — addresses the issue's explicit requirement to move prompt generation out of GHA
phases.pr_strategy: 2 PRs: one for the shared module + first 4 script migrations (T9-T10), one for remaining 3 scripts + orchestrator integration (T11-T12)

tasks.title: Create shared prompt builder Python module
tasks.description: Create shared/egg_prompts/ Python package with: (1) criteria.py — unified criteria loading with 3-tier fallback (.egg/ override → shared/prompts/ → inline fallback), porting the _read_shared_criteria() pattern. (2) conventions.py — conventions file loading for review, autofixer, and conflict conventions. (3) builders.py — prompt builder functions for each GHA prompt type (review, autofixer, agent-design-review, contract-verification, conflict, doc-updater, feedback). Each builder takes context parameters and returns prompt text. (4) cli.py — CLI entrypoint for GHA invocation (`python -m egg_prompts build-review --pr 123 --repo owner/name`). The module must work in both Docker containers and GHA runners with Python 3.12+. No Docker-specific or orchestrator-specific dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Module is importable as `from egg_prompts import builders`
Criteria loading supports 3-tier fallback chain identical to current _read_shared_criteria()
Conventions loading finds convention files relative to the action/ directory or accepts explicit paths
Each builder function accepts context dict and returns prompt string
CLI entrypoint supports all 7 prompt types with appropriate arguments
CLI outputs prompt-file path and model to stdout (for GHA GITHUB_OUTPUT integration)
No dependencies on orchestrator or Docker-specific packages
Unit tests exist for criteria loading, conventions loading, and each builder function
All tests pass
tasks.estimated_scope: large — new package with multiple modules, CLI, and tests

tasks.title: Migrate 4 criteria-sharing GHA scripts to Python
tasks.description: Convert the 4 GHA scripts that already use shared/prompts/ criteria files to thin bash wrappers calling the Python module: build-review-prompt.sh, build-autofixer-prompt.sh, build-agent-mode-design-review-prompt.sh, build-contract-verification-prompt.sh. Each bash script becomes a thin wrapper that: (1) validates required env vars, (2) calls `python3 -m egg_prompts <subcommand> --args...`, (3) captures the prompt-file path and model, (4) writes to GITHUB_OUTPUT. The Python builders must produce prompts equivalent to the current bash heredoc output. Create snapshot tests that capture current bash script output and verify Python produces equivalent content.
acceptance_criteria: Each bash script is a thin wrapper (under 30 lines) calling the Python module
Python builders produce prompts equivalent to the original bash heredoc output
Prompt-file and model GITHUB_OUTPUT interface is preserved
User override mechanism (.egg/ files) works identically through Python
Conventions files are loaded by Python, not bash
Existing action tests updated to test the Python implementations
Snapshot/equivalence tests verify no behavioral regression
All tests pass
tasks.estimated_scope: large — 4 scripts rewritten, test updates, equivalence verification

tasks.title: Migrate remaining 3 GHA scripts to Python
tasks.description: Convert the remaining 3 GHA scripts: build-conflict-prompt.sh (280 lines, most complex with multi-step git analysis context), build-doc-updater-prompt.sh (446 lines, complex context detection for file types and structure), build-feedback-prompt.sh (86 lines, simplest). The git analysis and context detection logic in conflict and doc-updater scripts needs careful translation—these scripts do shell-level git operations to gather context before building the prompt. The Python implementations should use subprocess calls for git operations or accept pre-computed context.
acceptance_criteria: Each bash script is a thin wrapper calling the Python module
Complex git analysis logic (conflict script) correctly translated to Python
Doc-updater context detection (file type analysis, structure detection) correctly translated
Prompt output is equivalent to original bash scripts
Existing action tests updated for Python implementations
All tests pass
tasks.estimated_scope: large — complex shell-to-Python translation, especially conflict and doc-updater scripts

tasks.title: Integrate shared module into orchestrator prompt builders
tasks.description: Refactor orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py to use the shared egg_prompts module for criteria and conventions loading. Replace the existing _read_shared_criteria(), _get_code_review_criteria(), _get_contract_review_criteria(), and _get_agent_design_criteria() functions with calls to egg_prompts.criteria. This eliminates duplicated fallback logic and ensures both systems use identical criteria loading. The orchestrator-specific prompt builders (_build_phase_prompt, _build_agent_prompt, _build_review_prompt, _build_checker_prompt, _build_autofix_prompt) remain in pipelines.py but delegate all criteria/conventions loading to the shared module.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator uses egg_prompts.criteria for all criteria loading
Orchestrator uses egg_prompts.conventions for conventions loading
Duplicated _read_shared_criteria() and related functions removed from pipelines.py
3-tier fallback chain works identically through the shared module
User override (.egg/) mechanism works the same
Orchestrator prompt tests updated and passing
All action tests still pass
No behavioral regression in orchestrator prompt output
tasks.estimated_scope: medium — refactor existing code to use new module, update tests

dependency_rationale.T10_depends_on_T9: Script migration uses the shared module created in T9

parallelism.notes: T1 and T2 are independent content edits. T4 and T5 can proceed in parallel once T3 is done. T6 (mission split) can proceed in parallel with T5 (GHA quality check) since they touch different files.

test_strategy.overall_approach: Every task must leave all existing tests passing. New functionality requires new tests. Prompt migration requires equivalence testing.

phase_1_content_audit.approach: Run existing test suites after each content change. No new test infrastructure needed—changes are content-only.
phase_1_content_audit.risk: Low — content changes don't affect test assertions unless tests assert on specific wording

phase_2_role_filtering.approach: New unit tests for the role-based filtering logic. Test each role's file set, default behavior, and pipeline-conditional rules.
phase_2_role_filtering.test_location: Determine from existing test structure—likely tests/sandbox/ or a new test file alongside entrypoint.py tests
test_cases: Each AgentRole gets correct file set
No role (default) produces full file set
Unknown role falls back to default
Pipeline-conditional rules only included when EGG_PIPELINE_ID is set AND role is appropriate
Generated CLAUDE.md content is valid markdown with proper separators

phase_3_prompt_unification.approach: Three layers: (1) Unit tests for shared module (criteria loading, conventions loading, builder functions). (2) Equivalence/snapshot tests comparing Python builder output to captured bash script output. (3) Integration tests verifying orchestrator uses shared module correctly.
phase_3_prompt_unification.test_location: shared/egg_prompts/tests/ for module tests; update tests/action/test_build_*.py for migration tests
test_cases: Conventions loading finds files at expected paths
Each builder produces well-formed prompt text
Python builder output matches original bash script output (equivalence)
CLI entrypoint writes prompt-file and outputs correct format
User override mechanism (.egg/) works through Python
Orchestrator criteria loading delegates to shared module

regression_testing.approach: Run the full test suite after every PR merge. The key invariant: no agent behavioral regression.

risks_and_mitigations.impact: Agent behavioral regression if Python prompts differ from bash originals
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Create snapshot tests capturing current bash output. Run both systems side-by-side during transition. Phase the migration (4 simpler scripts first, 3 complex ones second) to catch issues early.

risks_and_mitigations.impact: Agents fail tasks because they're missing instructions
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Conservative initial filtering: only remove clearly irrelevant files (e.g., pr-descriptions.md for non-coders). Default to full CLAUDE.md for unknown roles. Can always expand filtering later.

risks_and_mitigations.impact: External repos using egg action break
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Keep bash scripts as wrappers that preserve the interface (prompt-file and model outputs to GITHUB_OUTPUT). No workflow YAML changes needed.

risks_and_mitigations.impact: Wrapper scripts fail in GHA environment
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: GHA runners have Python 3.12 pre-installed. Add version check in wrapper scripts.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Large PR size for Phase 3 tasks
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Difficult to review, higher chance of issues
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Split into 2 PRs (PR-4 and PR-5). PR-4 establishes the pattern, PR-5 completes it.

open_questions_from_architect.question: Should orchestrator.md be included for ANY pipeline agent?
open_questions_from_architect.task_planner_recommendation: Agree with architect: include contract.md only for coder/tester/integrator/refiner. Trim orchestrator.md heavily (T2) and only include for coder/refiner. Most agents never call egg-orch directly.

open_questions_from_architect.question: Should slash command files be reconciled with orchestrator prompts?
open_questions_from_architect.task_planner_recommendation: Yes, reconcile during T3 and T5. The command files are the richer source—extract key guidance into orchestrator prompts. Keep both but ensure no contradictions. Document the relationship (command files = interactive use, orchestrator prompts = pipeline use).

open_questions_from_architect.question: Should conventions files be kept as markdown or moved to Python constants?
open_questions_from_architect.task_planner_recommendation: Keep as loadable markdown files within the shared module. Matches the existing pattern for shared/prompts/ criteria files. Easier to review and edit than Python string constants.
